title: Development Application — Submission to Approval
subtitle: Five stages, eight steps, four friction points, eight agents

inputs.label: The case, as it reaches the officer
inputs.description: A Qualified Person has submitted. What lands on the Processing Officer's desk is not a case — it is a pile of separate records, none of them reconciled.
inputs.inputFormat: Registration pack, fee invoice and receipt, lodged file set, federated model, survey plan, prior issues and the QP's response letter.

persona.quote: Every case starts with me rebuilding its history out of four systems and somebody's inbox.

inputs.label: What reaches the Approving Officer
inputs.description: At step 7 the Approving Officer gets a recommendation — and to test it, re-reads the case the PO has already read. Selecting the outcome is the statutory determination, and stays entirely theirs.
inputs.inputFormat: The PO's recommendation and formal issues, machine findings with their overrides and stated reasons, consultation replies, precedent.

persona.quote: I re-check what the officer already checked, because I cannot see what their conclusion rests on.

stations.label: SUBMISSION & CASE SETUP
stations.description: Steps 1–3. Lodge, publish, register and route. One agent on the registration and fee checks.

agents.name: A1 Registration & Fee Verification
agents.description: Background agent. Reconciles three accounts of one payment — what the guideline says is due, what the invoice charged, what the receipt settled — and names the difference in a sentence the officer can act on.
agents.output: Fee due beside fee paid, the provision it was derived from named, every line opening its source page. Readable in five seconds, checkable in thirty.

stations.label: PRE-VALIDATION
stations.description: Step 4. Validate the model and run the DC Assistant checks. The checks themselves stay untouched — they already work. One agent sits on top of them.

agents.name: A2 Submission Completeness & Geo-Reference Validation
agents.description: Background agent. Derives the document set this submission actually requires, works out what each lodged file really is, then diagnoses why the geo-reference failed — wrong datum, misplaced survey point, wrong lot, rotated model.
agents.output: Two panels for two questions: is it complete, and is it in the right place. The requirement list names the circular it came from, so the scoping can be challenged — not just the result.

stations.label: EVALUATION
stations.description: Steps 5–6. Review results, site history and consultations; consult other departments and agencies; formalise issues and recommend. The largest concentration of human steps in the workflow.

agents.name: A3 Submission Delta Review
agents.description: Interactive agent, fires on a resubmission. Only the model delta diffs cleanly — drawings, narrative and the response letter are prose no tool compares. The reconciliation is the answer, not the change list.
agents.output: Per prior issue: addressed, persisting, or not answered — plus what changed that nobody asked for. A contradiction between document and model is the finding that pays, because today it is found by accident.

agents.name: A4 Referral & Special Control
agents.description: Background agent. Not unstructured data — a variable path. Which internal team and which agency should see this case, and for which issue. The same site engages conservation but not urban design, depending on what is proposed.
agents.output: A routing proposal with a send button, not a notification — and a 'considered and not referred' list with reasons. Advisory only: nothing leaves URA until a person sends it.

agents.name: A5 Site Precedent Retrieval
agents.description: Hybrid agent — a background pre-brief, then chat. Answers 'have we seen this before, and what did we decide' — which nothing today can be asked. The archive is retrieve-by-reference: you need the case number to find the case.
agents.output: Cards, not search results, because the useful unit is a decision with its grounds attached: the outcome, the grounds, the condition imposed, whether it was appealed.

agents.name: A6 Issue Consolidation
agents.description: Interactive agent. Four vocabularies for one physical concern, with no shared field between them. It clusters by meaning, then does the harder thing — names the conflicts where two requirements cannot both be met.
agents.output: A board in three states: raw, clustered, needs a human. Every original comment stays in its own words and attributed. It surfaces a conflict; it must never resolve one.

stations.label: AO APPROVAL
stations.description: Step 7. The Approving Officer reviews the recommendation, the evidence and the overrides. The only stage with no automation at all today.

agents.name: A7 AO Briefing Pack
agents.description: Interactive agent. Answers 'what do I need to know before I look at this properly?' Breadth: what is proposed, what the site carries, what was found, who was consulted, what the PO recommends and why — every line cited.
agents.output: A document read top to bottom, with counts in the header and full lists always linked — because the failure mode of a summary is the thing it left out.

agents.name: A8 Evidence & Override Assurance
agents.description: Interactive agent. Answers 'can I rely on what I am being told?' Depth on one thing: every point a human departed from the machine result. Machine finding, override, stated reason and cited evidence, side by side.
agents.output: A matrix you sort and drill into. It reports completeness, never merits — 'this override cites a note that cannot be located' is a fact; whether it is justified stays with the AO.

outputs.label: Verified intake
outputs.value: Intake settled at the front door
outputs.description: Friction point 1 closed: registration, payment, files and geo-reference reconciled before evaluation begins.

outputs.label: Coordinated case
outputs.description: Friction point 2 closed: referrals, precedent and conflicting comments live in the record instead of an inbox.

outputs.label: Traceable decision
outputs.value: A decision that can be traced
outputs.description: Friction points 3 and 4 closed: the AO verifies instead of reconstructing, and the reasoning resolves to real sources.

steps.caption: The Processing Officer picks up the case. Fee, files and geo-reference each sit in a different record — and on a resubmission, the whole set is re-read by hand.
Downstream, the Approving Officer re-checks evidence the PO has already reviewed — because the link from findings and overrides to the recommendation is hard to trace.
The case enters the line the way it actually arrives: unreconciled, spread across systems, the reasoning still in people's heads and inboxes.
Submission and case setup. A1 reconciles what is due, what was charged and what was paid — and names where the difference arises.
Pre-validation. The model and rule checks already work, so they stay untouched. A2 sits on top of them: it derives the required document set and diagnoses why the geo-reference failed.
Evaluation — the largest concentration of human steps. A3 on the resubmission, A4 on referrals, A5 on precedent, A6 on the conflicting comments.
AO approval. A7 assembles the briefing pack and shows its own gaps. A8 audits whether each finding and override resolves to a real source. The AO verifies instead of reconstructing.
A1 and A2 turn four separate checks into one verdict — fee, files and geo-reference, each line opening its source.
A4, A5 and A6 put referrals, precedent and conflicts in the record — advisory, attributed, and never resolved on the agent's own authority.
A7 and A8 let the AO verify rather than reconstruct. Selecting the outcome carries no agent by design — it is the statutory determination.
